name: MO-07
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Eric Burlison running with large financial edge
Democrat Missi Hesketh raised only ~$50k with no outside support
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~96%
model.rationale: The R+21 district, Burlison's incumbency, and his roughly 29-to-1 fundraising advantage over Hesketh leave Democrats with no evident path; markets price a Republican win near 96%. The forecast stays essentially at the fundamentals, with only a token Democratic chance.
model.watch: A major outside-spending intervention or a scandal involving Burlison would be the main things to move this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Missouri's 7th District is one of the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent Eric Burlison was renominated and returns with roughly $958,000 on hand, while Democratic nominee Missi Hesketh has raised about $50,000 and has no outside spending on either side. A Libertarian also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Burlison about a 96% chance of winning. With the incumbent, the district lean, and the money gap all pointing the same way, this is a Safe Republican seat with only a nominal chance of an upset.
